top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, B050) is a single-writer proposal that I rank first on the common criteria, not on visible support. His voice is distinctive and recognisable in long, densely patterned sentences. The formal achievement lies in large, internally structured prose architectures, as publicly described in Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, where memory, the body and dream are built into one sustained metaphysical project. The poetic origin and the essays suggest a wider authorship, but I rely mainly on the major prose. The citation scope is clear: one writer, named Romanian language, prose and poetry. I do not treat the unanimity of round 2 as evidence of merit. Open reservations remain: whether the late volumes deepen or only repeat the project, how much of the Romanian syntax and rhythm survives translation, and thinner coverage of the poetry, essays and early prose. They argue for care about which volumes the citation relies on, not for withholding the prize. I see no merit or citation reason to prefer no award (P000), which I rank last. My judgments rest on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification.
